mechanisms.decisive_claim: For each prime p, checking the unique largest power p^j<=2n is sufficient for full carry freedom.
mechanisms.kill_test: Find n,p whose top-power remainder is below half but a lower-power remainder is above half.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Assigning p to the power nearest sqrt(n) yields a uniformly bounded reciprocal mass in every prime-power annulus.
mechanisms.kill_test: Evaluate annular reciprocal masses on exhaustive record n and primorial-adjacent adversaries; kill on growth with the number of annuli.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: The exact fixed-quotient intervals give an absolute bound for all carry-free primes p>sqrt(2n), including short terminal intervals.
mechanisms.kill_test: Replay exact primes at all interval endpoints and compare the sum with a direct Mertens bound.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Digit-block splitting gives f(n)<=C0+max_{m<=sqrt(n)} f(m), with every prime below sqrt(n) transferred injectively to the smaller argument.
mechanisms.kill_test: For every finite n, attempt all natural block maps and kill injectivity when two primes transfer inconsistently or the image prime is no longer carry-free.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Simultaneous carry-free events for distinct primes have pointwise density at most the product of their half-alphabet densities at every cutoff.
mechanisms.kill_test: Enumerate complete CRT periods for small prime sets and compare exact joint acceptance with the proposed product at every prefix cutoff.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: If carry freedom holds for primes p and q through enough digits, then the product of their effective moduli is O(n), limiting the total simultaneous reciprocal mass.
mechanisms.kill_test: Search n with long lower-half prefixes in several coprime bases and kill whenever the effective modulus product greatly exceeds n.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: A large-sieve bound for the nonzero Fourier modes of lower-half prime-power intervals gives a pointwise O(1) reciprocal acceptance sum.
mechanisms.kill_test: Compute exact small-modulus Fourier correlations and reject any claimed norm inequality missing diagonal or endpoint terms.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Under reciprocal-prime sampling, unresolved accepted mass loses a fixed fraction at each adaptive digit stopping level.
mechanisms.kill_test: Compute stopping profiles for record holders and CRT adversaries; kill if accepted mass can remain concentrated at arbitrarily many consecutive levels.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Descriptions of one n in many carry-free prime bases obey a mixed-radix Kraft inequality whose cost is proportional to sum 1/p.
mechanisms.kill_test: Test the proposed Kraft weights on all n in exact CRT periods; kill if code cylinders overlap with total weight above one.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: A weighted Selberg sieve over the missing Legendre jumps bounds the reciprocal mass of primes with zero total valuation uniformly in n.
mechanisms.kill_test: Replay candidate weights on exact valuations and kill negative coefficients, uncovered primes, or total weight growing like log log n.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: A recursive sieve on the first digit exceeding half either removes a fixed reciprocal mass or contracts all surviving primes to a common smaller integer problem.
mechanisms.kill_test: Partition exact accepted and rejected primes by first bad digit; kill if the surviving primes require mutually incompatible contracted integers.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Large-prime interval charging, a finite middle-scale Fourier certificate, and recursive treatment of small primes combine with constants independent of the number of scales.
mechanisms.kill_test: Write the complete loss ledger at both interfaces and kill if either boundary prime set is double-counted or leaves an O(log log n) residue.
